whatWasBuilt.oneLine: The Development services lens now refuses every personal name the live MyGov feeds carry, instead of rendering them, and its live licence rows come out in the design's own order - proven on the built surface by the ratified design instrument and by its own mutation harness.
filesInProduct: src/record-identity.mjs (NEW, 97 lines): the refusal rule and the reference format, in one place. REF_PREFIX per dimension (APP/HLD/OFF/INS/MGR), refusalBasis(dimension, field), opaqueRefs(dimension, values), refusedCount(values). References are numbered from the SORTED distinct values, not first-appearance, because first-appearance renumbers every reference when a feed returns its rows in a different order.

src/mygov-live.mjs: refuseNames() applies the refusal once per READ rather than once per row, so every case sharing an officer reads the same OFF-nn. composeRealInspections, composeRealCodeViolations and composeRealBusinessLicenses each declare `refuse: {...}`; composeRealBusinessLicenses also declares `order: compareLicenseRoll`. mapRealWorkOrderRecord's subject moves from `row.title` to `row.type`. mapRealCodeViolationRecord's assignedOfficer and mapRealInspectionRecord's inspector are nulled at the record, not only overridden at the field.
src/mygov-permits.mjs: composeRealPermits applies the applicant refusal; mapRealPermitRecord nulls the applicant.

src/domains/business-licenses.mjs: the fixture generator's band-then-expiry-offset comparator is extracted as `export function compareLicenseRoll()`, so the fixture path and the live path call ONE comparator and cannot drift (CTRL-1).
src/dev-services-naming.test.mjs (NEW, 18 tests in 6 suites): one test per acceptance item, each with a non-vacuity partner.

scripts/export-dev-services-lens.mjs (NEW): renders the lens for a pack into an arbitrary directory so the design check can read the built surface. `--base <url>` reads a deployed app; the manifest's `mode` field says `deployed`, `external-loopback` or `in-process`.

scripts/prove-dev-services-corrections.mjs (NEW): plants each of the four defects into an exported surface, one per mutant, and reports whether the check refuses each one and whether it still passes the unmutated control.
filesInDocRepo: _design/smartcity-dev-services/check.mjs: `--dir <path>` so the ratified instrument can be pointed at what the product renders. Plus the header-keyed, shape-free refusal rule for columns whose header names a person-or-business dimension (Applicant, Inspector, Officer, Subject), and self-tests for both. 54/54 self-tests, both directions.
whatWasBuilt.whatWasNotBuilt: No grant was added (OPS-17 A-147: MyGov is already granted at the KIND level and covers all five domains). No shared rendering in web/app.js or web/index.html was refactored, which the dispatch required while G-159 waited on this repo. No login or department-access control was built; G-143's finding that every signed-in account can open this lens is UNCHANGED, and it is the reason the refusals in this lane are refusals rather than permissions.

theRefusalIsARefusalNotAClassifier.doctrine: src/record-identity.mjs states it in its own header. The obvious rule - render a name unless it LOOKS like a person - does not survive the real strings. The capture this design was drawn from carries `DEBORAH MOORE, PH#737-762-6252` and `LISA BOE - CONTACT#: 504-401-1765`. The first is neither an all-caps name pair nor an initial-led name, so a regex tuned to either keeps it. In the other direction `Hill Country Homes` and `Deborah Ann Moore` have the SAME shape, so any test that keeps the first and drops the second is a guess wearing a rule's clothes.
theRefusalIsARefusalNotAClassifier.whatTheProductDoesInstead: The free-text field backs NO cell, and the record states why: `the applicant is an opaque reference; row.applicant is the vendor's free-text field and is not rendered on this surface, because a name beside an address is published to every department`.
theRefusalIsARefusalNotAClassifier.theBasisTravelsWithTheRecord: nameRefusedBasis is written on every affected record, so the absence is stated on the record rather than being a blank a reader has to interpret.
theRefusalIsARefusalNotAClassifier.theBusinessExceptionIsTheDesigns: A business on a licence is a commercial entity and a public record, so naming one names no person; that is the design folder's rule, restated in the design README, and this lane did not widen or narrow it.

theRepeatOffenderDecision.question: The dispatch asks: the code-violation mapper passes an `isRepeatOffender` flag beside each address - decide against the design whether it belongs on the surface where it lands, and say why.
theRepeatOffenderDecision.measuredFirst: Where it lands was measured, not assumed: `isRepeatOffender` appears in exactly ONE place in this repo - the mapper line that reads it (src/mygov-live.mjs). The Code enforcement row builder reads recordId, violationType, place, status, escalationStep, assignedOfficer/officerRef and reportedDate. The design folder draws no such column on any of its six artboards.
theRepeatOffenderDecision.reason: Not only that the design does not draw it. A repeat-offender flag is a JUDGEMENT ABOUT A RESIDENT, computed from the vendor's own case history and presented beside that resident's address, on a screen the dispatch records as open to EVERY signed-in department because department access is not enforced (G-143). An operational fact - this case is at rung 3 - is a staff fact; a characterisation of the person living at the address is not. The cheapest place to keep it off is where it is already not read, so the field is carried on the record and backs no cell.
theRepeatOffenderDecision.lockedByTest: src/dev-services-naming.test.mjs: 'lands on no rendered field, and it is not added to one'. The row builder's read list is restated in the test, so the day a column is added the field list has to be edited in the same commit.

threeInstrumentsWereMeasuringThemselves.oneLine: Reaching the live proof exposed four defects, three of them in the proving tools rather than the product, and each had been returning a confident wrong answer rather than an error.
threeInstrumentsWereMeasuringThemselves.theSettleConditionWasSatisfiedByTheWrong: The exporter waited on the SUM of every queue's children. Every Development services tab renders all five queues, so a populated Pipeline queue satisfied the condition on the first snapshot - FOR EVERY TAB. Six tabs were reported settled that had never been waited on, the Licences queue was recorded as 0 rows, and the check refused a verdict on the empty roll. The live app serves 73 business licences for bastrop_tx. It now waits on the tab it just opened.
threeInstrumentsWereMeasuringThemselves.theFinalCaptureWasTakenOnTheWrongTab: The single-file design rested on 'the lens renders all five region queues into the document at load'. Measured: a Development services tab does, but the two non-domain tabs leave them EMPTY, and the sweep ended on flood-study - so the artifact written was 33KB of empty queues. The sweep is now followed by a return to a domain tab, and the settle loop waits for POPULATED then stable, because 'unchanged across two polls' is satisfied by two consecutive zeros, which is an unread surface rather than a settled one.
threeInstrumentsWereMeasuringThemselves.thePeopleRuleNamedASitusSentinelAsAPerso: It reported 'table cells name people [TX USA]' on the live surface. Live permits carry a situs that is nothing but the state and country suffix - no street, no city - and the all-caps alternation that exists to catch 'DEBORAH MOORE' matches any two all-caps tokens, so it named four rows of sentinel addresses as persons. NOT A PII LEAK; a false positive. The fix names the sentinel vocabulary (US state codes and 'USA') rather than relaxing the name shapes, and asserts both directions: 'DEBORAH MOORE' and 'DANA MOORE' are still refused. This is the P-214/X9 bare-situs class arriving in this lens.
threeInstrumentsWereMeasuringThemselves.theOrderRuleDemandedGlobalMonotonicity: It required globally non-decreasing expiry offsets. The design's own comparator - compareLicenseRoll, EXPORTED BY THE PRODUCT - sorts by status severity FIRST and by offset within that band. A revoked licence carrying a 2021 expiry belongs after the active band by design, so its offset is legitimately lower than the block before it, and the check FAILED a correct live surface. It now reads the roll row by row and requires the bands to appear in the product's own severity order AND the offsets to be non-decreasing within a band - strictly STRONGER than the rule it replaces. Band ranks are read from LICENSE_STATUS_VALUES, where every unrecognised status collapses to ONE SHARED LAST RANK; giving each unknown status its own rank made the rule fire wherever two interleaved, which on bastrop_tx is most of the roll.
threeInstrumentsWereMeasuringThemselves.theLesson: Every one of these produced a plausible reading of a real artifact. None produced an error. The only thing that caught them was pointing the tool at live data and reading the numbers rather than the exit code - which is exactly what the dispatch's OPS-17 A-146 argument predicted a demo pack cannot do.

THE DECOMPOSITION THAT MADE THIS LANE'S PROOF HARD IS WORTH KNOWING: the four corrections are LIVE-DATA facts, the instrument needs a BUILT surface, the built surface with live data needs a DEPLOYED app, and the deployed app's bastrop pack needs a credentialed browser.
